text: Paper Sec. 5.2.2 Eq. (8) and Algorithm 2 integrate both path length and deviation over the full forest T (T=r*t). Official algorithms/dif.py:L245-L275 averages per-representation scores; _cal_score at L454-L463 first computes a depth exponential times mean deviation within each six-tree representation forest. These expressions are generally unequal. Follow the paper: aggregate path lengths and deviations over all r*t trees, then multiply the two terms.

Paper Sec. 5.2.2 Eq. (7) and Algorithm 2 define the arithmetic mean of absolute split deviations over the traversed split nodes, including exact-zero deviations in the node count. Official algorithms/dif.py:L420-L421 instead counts only nonzero deviations and adds 1e-6. Follow the paper: divide by the number of visited internal split nodes; define deviation as zero for a tree with no split nodes.

Paper Sec. 5.2.2 Eq. (8), Sec. 5.3 and Algorithm 2 use the recorded traversed path length |p| and do not specify a terminal-leaf correction. Official algorithms/dif.py:L396-L399 adds c(n_samples_leaf) to the number of traversed edges. Follow the literal paper definition: use traversed edge count without adding the leaf-population correction. Retain standard iForest c(sample_size) as the score normalizer, whose numerical implementation is supplied by official code.

Paper Sec. 6.1.4 reports threshold-free AUC-ROC and AUC-PR without specifying label-based segment adjustment. Official utils.py:L199-L220 and L268-L281 replace scores within labeled anomalous segments by the segment maximum and return adjusted metrics, also computing best-test-label F1 in L135-L149. The reproduction returns raw DEAS scores and delegates all thresholding, adjustment and metrics to the fixed EasyTSAD/LiveLeaderBoard evaluator; it never reads test labels.

Use independent CNNs for the time-series backbone, following main_ts.py:L39-L48 (new_ensemble_method=0) and algorithms/dif.py:L214-L229. Paper Sec. 5.2.1 derives CERE using layer weight matrices and Sec. 5.4.1 analyzes its MLP implementation, but gives no concrete CERE convolutional implementation for time series; Sec. 6.1.3 only specifies the TS2Vec-like dilated residual CNN. Do not transfer the tabular MLP CERE setting to the CNN.

Official algorithms/dif.py:L280-L303 fits StandardScaler separately on the entire representation collection in each deep_transfer call, then applies tanh. Because _inference_transfer at L232-L243 calls deep_transfer again for time series, test representations are standardized using their own collection statistics, independently of training statistics. Preserve this algorithm-internal, label-free behavior because the paper is silent; do not silently replace it with train-fitted scaling. Raw-input preprocessing remains raw.

Neither paper nor main_ts.py/utils.get_sub_seqs specifies handling a split shorter than the 100-point window. Neutral default: require at least window_size observations in each split used for fitting/scoring and raise an informative error otherwise; do not shorten the window, fabricate observations, or silently change the architecture.

For trees with no internal split nodes, Eq. (7) is undefined. Neutral convention: path length=0 and mean deviation=0, yielding zero contribution to the deviation average; if the forest normalizer c(min(max_samples,n_train_windows)) is zero, return zero anomaly scores. This is consistent with no available isolation evidence and the zero-filled deviation arrays / skipped one-node trees in algorithms/dif.py:L355-L370, while avoiding the official 0/0 in L454.

IMPLEMENT uses the existing torch2 environment, verified via scripts/tsad run DIFR: torch 2.6.0+cu124, numpy 1.26.4, sklearn 1.9.1; CUDA is available. Registered DIFR exactly once in envs/registry.toml. No packages or shared environment metadata were changed. The standalone TS source omits graph imports and preserves upstream Apache-2.0 license and attribution.

Implementation-only adaptations: contiguous windows are generated lazily (same starts and float32 values); scipy-backed sklearn sparse decision paths accumulate visited internal-node counts and absolute gaps without the official dense sample-by-all-tree-nodes matrices. Network weights are frozen and eval() is used; the CNN has no active dropout or batch normalization, so these changes preserve forward values. All paper-vs-code scoring choices remain exactly those already approved in the contract.

The first self-test invocation via python -m EasyTSAD.Methods.DIFR.selftest failed before executing the method because the existing EasyTSAD.Methods -> DataFactory -> Controller -> Methods import cycle requires Controller to be imported first. scripts/tsad.py:L157 documents and applies that same requirement for managed import checks. The harness import check already passes. Rerun self-test with an entrypoint that imports EasyTSAD.Controller first; do not modify the fixed framework.

Completed IMPLEMENT self-test passed in registered torch2 on CPU with the full configured 50-network/300-tree ensemble on small random data. Verified all 27 config-key claims for exact value equality, unique torch2 registration, UTS/MTS fitting and score suffix shape, an independent literal root-to-leaf full-forest Eq. (8) reference, exact per-network seed/weight initialization, repeatability, zero gaps, constant trees, single-window forests, and short-input errors. The initial import-order-only failure was resolved by preloading Controller, as the normal runner does. mcp__tsad__check_method reports ok for DIFR. No dataset evaluation or parameter tuning was performed.

Input validation requires finite numeric observations and raises an informative ValueError rather than imputing or transforming NaN/Inf. This is an operational precondition for the fixed random-CNN/sklearn algorithm, not extra input normalization. The lazy windows convert to float32 at batch input, matching official batch_x.float().
